historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (15.65%) is >30% above revenue 5-year CAGR (9.7%) and matches EPS CAGR (16.45%, split-adjusted) rather than through-cycle business growth; book equity is also distorted by Lam returning most FCF via buybacks ($32.6bn of treasury stock against $13.9bn of equity). Revenue CAGR is used as the through-cycle anchor instead, and even that is measured into an upcycle year.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs are FY2023->FY2026 and FY2021->FY2026. FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2021 2,999.2, FY2023 4,251.8, FY2026 4,308.7. Owner-FCF CAGR runs ~1pp below reported FCF CAGR: SBC plus interest income grew slightly faster than cash flow, a small effect at SBC of ~1.7% of revenue. FY2026 FCF is depressed by a $1.96bn receivables build; TTM reported FCF to 2026-09-27 is ~$6.54bn on TTM revenue of ~$26.1bn. EPS CAGRs use split-adjusted figures (FY2021 26.90/10 = 2.69).

scenario_narratives.base: The AI/HBM build-out delivers what is already visible - FY2027 revenue near $34bn on a first half that is reported and guided, and one more year of growth as CY2027 WFE clears $200bn - and then behaves like every prior WFE cycle. Memory makers digest HBM and DRAM capacity, foundry leading-edge adds slow, and China (34-35% of revenue, guided below 30%) keeps shrinking under export controls and domestic substitution; revenue falls ~22% over FY2029-FY2030 before resuming growth on GAA logic, 3D NAND and advanced packaging content gains, with CSBG (36% of revenue) cushioning the trough. Lam keeps its structural gross-margin gains, so mid-cycle adjusted EBITDA settles at 39% against 33-36% in FY2024-FY2025; cash tax drifts from 17% to 21% as the Malaysia incentive runs off. FY2036 revenue of ~$42bn is a 6% CAGR from FY2026 and assumes WFE in the mid-2030s is not much larger than the 2027 peak.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI is a step change in the level of WFE, not a cycle peak. HBM and leading-edge logic keep raising deposition and etch intensity per wafer, Lam gains share at the GAA, backside-power, dry-EUV-resist (Aether) and advanced-packaging inflections, and US/Taiwan/Korea fab build-outs fully replace lost China revenue. There is a pause (FY2029 +3%) but no downturn; revenue reaches ~$64bn by FY2036 (10.7% CAGR from FY2026). Operating leverage and a growing installed-base business hold adjusted EBITDA at 42-45%, and the Malaysia incentive is renewed or replaced so cash tax settles at 19%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The AI capex wave turns out to be over-built and China closes at the same time. Hyperscaler spending pauses, HBM/DRAM pricing breaks and Lam's four large customers (Micron, Samsung, SK hynix, TSMC) cut capex together in FY2028; wider export controls (Hua Hong-style shipment halts, Entity List additions) and AMEC/Naura substitution take most of the remaining China systems business, and Tokyo Electron wins share where US vendors cannot ship. Second-half FY2027 revenue is flat on Q1, then revenue falls ~37% peak to trough to ~$21bn and recovers only at 3-6% to ~$27bn by FY2036. Under-absorbed factories and a protected R&D budget (~10% of revenue) compress adjusted EBITDA to 32-35%, and cash tax rises to 23% as the incentive expires under a global minimum tax.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Lam is a high-quality, high-ROIC cyclical valued at what looks like peak earnings. The model accepts the visible FY2027 step-up but refuses to capitalise it: the terminal year is a mid-cycle year with normal margins and an unsheltered tax rate, discounted at a 10.5% rate with a Gordon multiple of ~13-15x owner FCF. On that basis the stock price sits well above even the bull case; the market is paying for the AI upcycle to be a permanent level shift with a growth multiple on top. Because SBC is only ~1.7% of revenue, the house/street band is narrow - the gap to the price is about cycle and multiple, not accounting regime.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cycle timing and depth: the base case's FY2029-FY2030 correction is a judgment; if WFE plateaus instead of falling (bull path), value roughly doubles versus base
Structural WFE level: if AI lifts mid-2030s WFE far above the 2027 peak, FY2036 revenue of ~$42bn is too low
China: 34-35% of revenue under expanding export controls; guided below 30% for CY2026, with domestic toolmakers taking share
Terminal multiple: Gordon at 10.5%/3% is ~13.7x FCF, well below the 20-30x earnings the market has paid for Lam; the valuation is conservative by construction on this axis
Tax: the Malaysia incentive was worth $968m in FY2026 (~$0.77 of EPS); terminal cash tax of 21% (base) versus 12-17% today is a ~5-10% swing in terminal FCF
Flat share count: Lam retires ~1.5% of shares a year with cash far in excess of SBC, which the flat-count convention does not credit
Working capital: -15% capture on revenue change is an estimate; FY2026 consumed ~$2bn of receivables on a $4.8bn revenue increase

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 135.5-438.5
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL via research/LRCX/Reports/LRCX_Metrics.csv (FY2009-Q1 FY2027); FY2026 Form 10-K (LRCX_Annual_FY2026.txt) for SBC, D&A, tax, Malaysia incentive and working-capital lines; Q1 FY2027 Form 10-Q (LRCX_Quarterly_Q1-2027.txt) for the 2026-09-27 balance sheet, diluted shares, cover-page share count and quarter cash flow
data_sources.qualitative: research/LRCX/Reports/LRCX_Analysis.json (2026-11-15): Q2 FY2027 guidance, CY2026/CY2027 WFE outlook, China mix guidance, $25bn buyback authorisation

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: Q1 FY2027 10-Q diluted weighted-average shares (1,255.768m, quarter ended 2026-09-27). Cover page shows 1,249.171m basic shares outstanding at 2026-10-20; the ~6.6m gap is the treasury-method dilution. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). Split-adjusted basis only (10-for-1 split; pre-FY2023 CSV share counts and EPS are NOT split-adjusted and were divided by 10 for the EPS CAGR).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement, 'Equity-based compensation expense' $386,381k (LRCX_Annual_FY2026.txt:2482; restated in the equity-plan note at :2757). Lam publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding figure: cash taxes on net-share settlement are buried inside 'Treasury stock purchases' ($3,851m FY2026) and are not separately disclosed, so the add-back is used as-is and the forward SBC % path is held at or above the latest actual run-rate (Q1 FY2027: 1.40% of revenue) as an allowance.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 10.5% USD house rate for US technology: ~4.3% US 10-year risk-free + ~1.35 beta x ~4.6% ERP on an essentially all-equity capital structure ($3.7bn fixed-rate notes against a ~$280bn market cap). The same WACC is used in all three scenarios: semiconductor-capex cyclicality, China export-control risk and customer concentration are charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, not again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP filer: operating lease cost is already an operating expense inside EBITDA; finance lease obligations are inside 'long-term debt and finance lease obligations' and therefore in total_debt. No further lease adjustment.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, three probability-weighted scenarios (dcf-methods routing: operating company, cyclical). Lam is a wafer-fab-equipment maker; value is a stream of free cash flow, so the default engine applies. CYCLICAL FRAMING: FY0 is FY2026 (revenue $23.2bn). FY2027 is modelled off the reported Q1 ($8.22bn) plus the December-quarter guide (~$8.6bn), i.e. a first half already near $16.8bn. The AI/HBM upcycle is NOT extrapolated: base and bear both run a post-peak WFE correction inside the explicit period, and the terminal year (FY2036) is built as a mid-cycle year - mid-cycle revenue, mid-cycle margin, and a cash tax rate with the Malaysia incentive expired - so the terminal value capitalises a normal year, not a peak. Terminal cap is 15x (cyclical band), though Gordon binds below it in every scenario. OWNER FCF: last_fcf = reported FCF 4,891.3 - SBC 386.4 - interest income 196.2 = 4,308.7. Interest income is stripped (gross cash $7.4bn is added in the bridge; flows are unlevered so interest expense on the notes is likewise excluded). FY2026 FCF was depressed by a $1.96bn receivables build on the revenue ramp; the forward build does not carry the FY2026 margin - it is rebuilt from components. WORKING CAPITAL: negative capture (-15% of the revenue CHANGE): receivables + inventory far exceed payables + deferred profit (net ~26% of FY2026 revenue), so growth consumes cash and a downturn releases it. TAX: FY2026 GAAP rate 12.1%, cash taxes paid $1,334m (~16% of EBIT); Q1 FY2027 GAAP rate 16.9% on the higher NCTI rate. The Malaysia 15-year incentive (effective FY2022, so expiring ~FY2036) cut FY2026 tax by $968m; base ramps the cash rate to 21% by the terminal year rather than perpetuating the shelter. BUYBACKS: funded repurchaser - FY2026 treasury purchases of $3.85bn are ~10x the SBC charge, so the flat share count is conservative (the count has been falling ~1.5%/yr); a new $25bn authorisation was announced 2026-11-05 but only cash actually spent is recorded. ANCHOR VINTAGE: net cash and diluted shares are from the 2026-09-27 balance sheet while Year 1 is all of FY2027, so Q1 FY2027 free cash flow retained after buybacks and dividends (~$1.9bn, ~$1.5/share) is counted in both; this is more than offset by end-of-year discounting of a fiscal year already ~38% elapsed at the valuation date. The $1.0bn September 2026 ASRs settle in the December quarter and will trim the count slightly. The price is a regular-session close; the stock is highly volatile (52-week range 135.5-438.5), so the upside figure is unusually sensitive to the print date.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 ~$34.4bn: Q1 $8.22bn reported + Q2 ~$8.6bn guided + a second half near $8.8bn/quarter on the CY2027 WFE >$200bn outlook. FY2028 +8% to a ~$37bn peak, then a two-year correction (-22% peak to trough; FY2023->FY2024 was -14.5% off a far smaller boom) and recovery at 9% fading to 4%. FY2036 revenue ~$42bn = 6.1% CAGR from FY2026.
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA = GAAP operating income + D&A + SBC. Actuals: FY2024 33.0%, FY2025 36.0%, FY2026 38.9%, Q1 FY2027 42.8%. Mid-cycle 39% keeps the structural gross-margin gain (46% -> 52%) but gives back peak operating leverage.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: there is no balance-sheet risk, but the downside rests on two live, largely independent threats - a single-regulator dependency on roughly a third of revenue (US export controls on China) and an AI capex cycle the company itself flags as reversible - and the business has a long record of 15-40% revenue drawdowns. Base held at 50%: a boom followed by a normal WFE correction is the pattern of every prior cycle. Bull cut to 25%: it needs several things to go right at once - no downturn for a decade after a +50% year, share gains at every inflection, China fully replaced, and a tax shelter extended.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
